skips: Three opt-in real-model tests were not run

capability_modes.partial: approximate gaze observation only; head control when a neutral point exists
capability_modes.none: phone, face monitoring and exam-window protection remain available; no gaze/head auto-stop

regressions: Zero-point, partial, failed and full starts preserve only the capabilities actually available at session start
Accepted calibration groups survive cancel, failure and timeout; unfinished samples are discarded
A partial or approximate gaze signal cannot trigger gaze removal, while a saved center can control head pose independently
Phone removal remains independent of calibration and uses the first fresh recognized frame
A later full-looking camera state cannot upgrade a partial session
Reports describe the saved calibration mode and accepted point count, including historical reports
A participant reset clears the previous calibration; a stale cancellation ID cannot affect a newer calibration
limitations: Synthetic camera observations; no physical user camera or native Windows verification
Approximate partial gaze is observation-only and does not prove where a person looked
Measured uncertainty is not a confidence probability and cannot guarantee zero false positives
Actual FPS and model behavior depend on the user's camera, drivers and laptop
